accuracy.evidence: Names are generated by a lowest-locant rule (min(p, n+1−p)) and checked by hand: CH₃CHBrCH₃ is 2-bromopropane, Br on carbon 3 of butane is 2-bromobutane, methane and ethane need no number. Bond enthalpies use the common A-level mean values C–F 467, C–Cl 346, C–Br 290, C–I 228 kJ/mol, and the text says sources vary. Chemguide's halogenoalkane pages confirm that bond strength, not polarity, sets the rate, and give the silver nitrate colours (AgI yellow first, AgBr cream, AgCl white last). The ozone steps Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂ and ClO• + O₃ → Cl• + 2O₂ net to 2O₃ → 3O₂. The ammonia conditions (excess NH₃ in ethanol, sealed tube) and the NH₄Br by-product are correct.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the known slips: numbering from the far end (the step 1 prediction offers 3-bromobutane, there is a 'num' challenge tag, and p1/m1), thinking the most polar bond reacts fastest (step 3 prediction trap, refusal text on a wrong ranking, 'polar' challenge tags, p5), thinking a nucleophile attacks the δ− halogen (step 2 prediction, refusal on drop, 'sign' tags, m2), thinking C–F breaks in CFCs (refused bond tap, 'cf' tag, m5), thinking Cl• is used up (step 5 prediction, 'used' tag, m8) and mixing up the ozone hole with heat or global warming ('warm' tag, adult text).

lab_distinct.evidence: The learner builds named molecules by choosing a halogen and tapping a carbon, with the name and condensed formula updating live. They drag OH⁻ and then NH₃ onto the δ+ carbon to make ethanol and ethylamine, rank three silver nitrate tubes before warming them, tap the bond UV breaks in CCl₂F₂, and drag one radical across a field of O₃. flagchlor covers radical substitution of alkanes and flaghal covers group 7 displacement; neither names haloalkanes, does nucleophilic substitution or runs the ozone cycle, and gate_lab_distinct passes against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule appears through action before the text states it. Placing Br on C3 of butane shows the name 2-bromobutane. Dropping OH⁻ on bromine is refused with 'OH⁻ is drawn to the δ+ carbon, not the δ− bromine'. A wrong tube ranking is played out, so the learner sees iodo cloud first, and is then told the weakest bond breaks first, with the bond enthalpies under each tube. Tapping C–F is refused with its 467 kJ/mol value. The ozone counter keeps climbing while the label switches Cl• → ClO• → Cl•, so the learner sees the catalyst at work.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the step then tests: 3-bromobutane against 2-bromobutane, attacking the δ− bromine against the δ+ carbon, the most polar chloroalkane against iodoalkane as fastest, CFCs 'lighter than air' against unreactive as the reason they reach the ozone layer, and Cl• 'used up' against going on to destroy more. All of them are answered by what the learner does straight after, not by text alone.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The Challenge alternates generated naming questions (propane and butane, with Cl, Br or I at different positions; distractors with the far-end number and the wrong stem) with seven conceptual questions. Each wrong option has its own explanation: polarity versus bond enthalpy, elimination with hot ethanolic OH⁻, adding versus replacing, δ signs, C–F strength, the Cl• catalyst, ozone loss not being heating, and why HFCs are ozone-safe. Naming items also add a counting tip, and there is a streak counter.

readability.evidence: The kid explanation scores Flesch–Kincaid grade 4.2, inside the 6.5 learner target, using short sentences and defining nucleophile, δ+ and radical where they first appear. The adult text scores 9.1, inside the 9.5 target, and keeps the IUPAC naming rules, conditions and bond enthalpy data. Canvas headings are short, and every line of status text wraps inside the canvas width on a 390 px phone.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a fact the learner uses: the naming rule with a worked name, the δ+ carbon and two real substitutions with their conditions, the bond enthalpy order with the silver nitrate colours, and the CFC route to the stratosphere with the two radical equations. There are no generic openers or banned filler words, and the content gate's similarity check passes against all other lessons.

mobile.evidence: Every canvas action also has a full-width button: halogen and carbon pickers, nucleophile to carbon or bromine, one button per tube, one per CFC bond, and 'hits next O₃'. Canvas hit radii are 30–44 px, the drag targets are large balls, and the browser gate's iPhone 13 walkthrough finished every step with no horizontal scroll. The tube labels shrink to fit on narrow widths.

accessibility.evidence: The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the current name, formula, product or equation, and c.say announces the same text. All controls are real buttons with aria-labels such as 'Put it on carbon 2' and 'Use bromo'. Challenge feedback sits in a polite live region, and the colours (green Cl, brown Br, purple I, white, cream and yellow precipitates) are always paired with text labels. axe-core reports no serious or critical issues.
